text: Atomicity means a transaction is all or nothing. Consistency means the database moves from one valid state to another and keeps its constraints true. Isolation means concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other. Durability means committed data persists even after a crash.

Atomic: all-or-nothing execution, so in a bank transfer both the debit and the credit happen or neither does. Consistent: constraints such as a non-negative balance remain valid after commit. Isolated: concurrent transactions behave as if they ran one after another. Durable: once committed the data is permanent even if the server crashes.

ACID guarantees reliable transactions. Atomicity ensures all or nothing, durability ensures committed data is permanent, isolation prevents concurrent transactions from interfering, and consistency preserves integrity constraints.

A transaction is atomic so a failure midway rolls everything back. It is consistent because constraints hold before and after. It is isolated so concurrent transactions cannot interfere, and durable so committed changes persist after a crash.
